tool.name: Create IDR pseudoreplicates
tool.description: split a BAM into two complementary, mate-preserving partitions

param.name: input_bam
param.label: Input BAM
param.help: A filtered BAM for one replicate, or a BAM made by merging replicates.

param.name: seed
param.label: Random seed
param.help: The same BAM and seed always produce the same two complementary partitions.

tool.help:
**What it does**
This tool creates the two complementary pseudoreplicates needed by an IDR ChIP-seq workflow. Every BAM alignment is assigned to exactly one output. Assignment is based on a reproducible keyed hash of the complete query name.
Because all records with the same query name receive the same assignment, paired reads, secondary alignments, and supplementary alignments remain in the same pseudoreplicate. Both outputs are coordinate-sorted, validated, and indexed.
The split is random-like and approximately 50/50. It is not guaranteed to have exactly the same number of records in both outputs. For normal ChIP-seq library sizes, the relative difference is expected to be small.
**IDR usage**
For pooled pseudoreplicates, first merge all ChIP BAMs together and all matched control BAMs together. Run this tool independently on the pooled ChIP BAM and the pooled control BAM, using a recorded seed. Call peaks on corresponding partitions (ChIP 1 versus control 1, ChIP 2 versus control 2), then compare the two peak lists with IDR.
For self-consistency, run the tool separately on each biological replicate and its matched control.
Do not replace this operation with two independent 50% downsampling jobs: those would overlap and would not form complementary partitions.
